Dubai Islamic Bank (DIB) to acquire Emirates Islamic in $8.5 bn deal
sum: Dubai Islamic Bank (DIB) has agreed to acquire Emirates Islamic Bank from Emirates NBD in an all-share transaction that will create one of the world’s largest listed Islamic banking groups and strengthen DIB’s position as the UAE’s largest Sharia-compliant lender.

Under the agreement, DIB will issue 3.49 bn new shares to Emirates NBD in exchange for 100% of Emirates Islamic’s issued share capital, according to a joint announcement published on the Dubai Financial Market on November 25, 2026.
- Dubai Islamic Bank has agreed to acquire 100% of Emirates Islamic Bank through an all-share transaction valued at AED31.1 bn ($8.5 bn).
- The combined banking group will have assets of AED585 bn ($159.2 bn), becoming the world’s second-largest Islamic lender behind Saudi Arabia’s Al Rajhi Bank.
- The acquisition remains subject to regulatory approval, with operational integration, branch consolidation and customer migration expected to follow completion.

The transaction values Emirates Islamic at approximately AED31.1 bn ($8.5 bn), based on DIB’s closing share price. The combined institution will have assets of AED585 bn ($159.2 bn), ranking second globally among Islamic banks by assets, behind Saudi Arabia’s Al Rajhi Bank. The acquisition requires regulatory approval, including clearance from the Central Bank of the UAE and the Capital Markets Authority.
This transaction represents an important opportunity for Dubai to … further strengthen the emirate’s position as a global centre for Islamic finance.

Financial close reached on $2.1bn Taweelah C power plant
sum: Abu Dhabi National Energy Company (TAQA), in partnership with Emirates Water and Electricity Company (EWEC), Sembcorp Industries, and Aljomaih Energy and Water Company, has announced the financial close of the Dh7.76bn ($2.1bn) Taweelah C Independent Power Producer (IPP) project.

The plant, which will be situated approximately 50km northeast of Abu Dhabi within the Al Taweelah Power and Desalination Complex, is expected to deliver a capacity of 2.6GW using a combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) configuration.
The project is being financed primarily through senior debt arranged by several local and international banks.

These include the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation, Development Bank of Singapore, KfW International Project and Export Finance Bank, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, and First Abu Dhabi Bank.
Dubai Islamic Bank and Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank also participated in coordinating and arranging the transaction.
EWEC, TAQA, and the consortium previously signed a power purchase agreement making EWEC the sole purchaser of the plant's electricity.
TAQA holds a 60% equity stake in the project company, with the remaining 40% owned by the international partners.

Dubai weighs Islamic bank mega-merger
sum: Good morning, everyone. Dubai could be about to build one of the world’s biggest Islamic banks. Dubai Islamic Bank and Emirates Islamic are reportedly weighing a merger that would create a lender with c. AED 585 bn in assets. It would be Dubai’s first combination of two large banks since Emirates NBD was formed in 2007. The DIB and Emirates NBD boards both meet tomorrow, so we may not have to wait long to find out more.
In mining, IRH is moving in on Irish titanium miner Kenmare, offering a 52% premium for a company that needs the money. Mubadala, meanwhile, sold its entire stake in Canada’s Barrick Mining in 3Q.

On the energy side of things, a TAQA-led consortium reached financial close for the 2.6 GW Taweelah C plant with AED 7.76 bn lined up for the gas-fired plant, which is slated for commercial operations in 2029.

Plus: Mubadala Capital showed up as an anchor investor for an M&G growth fund that raised USD 900 mn at its first close, and Omniyat’s Beyond Developments has an AED 80 bn masterplan for Yardlands in Dubai.

But first: would you like to have lunch with us on Thursday, 10 December? We’re setting a table in DIFC for a very small and exclusive group of readers and business leaders in the UAE. If you’d like to be there, just hit reply to this email, tell us who you are and what you do, and we’ll take it from there.

Wait, lunch? Yes, lunch. Two hours, one table, no panel, no slides, just an open conversation among peers. We want to hear how the people running businesses in the UAE see the next twelve months: what’s working, what’s getting harder, and where the money is actually going now that the region is open for business again. Expect good food, good company, and the kind of conversation nobody has on stage.
Seats will be strictly limited and the lunch is invitation-only, but we’re planning on doing this more often.

Dubai Islamic Bank shares surge 11% on potential acquisition deal
sum: Dubai Islamic Bank shares closed 11 per cent higher on Monday after the lender said its board would meet this week to evaluate a strategic acquisition, amid reports of talks to combine it with Emirates Islamic, the Sharia-compliant unit of Emirates NBD.

The lender’s board will be holding a meeting on Wednesday to discuss the matter, the UAE’s biggest Sharia-compliant bank said in a brief statement on Monday to the Dubai Financial Market, where its shares are traded. It did not provide further details.

Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, said officials have held preliminary talks on combining the two lenders. However, it added no final decision had been made and a deal may not materialise.

Emirates NBD, in a separate statement, said its board would meet the same day to “consider and approve potential transaction opportunities”. It also did not provide further details. Its shares were down 0.8 per cent at the end of trading on Monday.

If the transaction goes ahead, this would be one of the biggest mergers in the banking industry in the UAE following the merger of Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank with Union National Bank and Al Hilal Bank in 2019.
National Bank of Abu Dhabi was combined with First Gulf Bank to create First Abu Dhabi Bank in 2017.

Established in 1975, DIB is the largest Islamic bank in the UAE by assets. With group assets exceeding Dh427 billion ($116.27 billion) by the end of September, the bank has a workforce of about 12,000 employees and more than 540 branches in the Middle East, Asia and Africa.

Turkey's TPAO is in talks to borrow up to USD 1 bn, with Gulf banks in the mix
sum: Turkey’s state-owned oil and gas producer TPAO is in talks with banks to borrow up to USD 1 bn to fund projects at home and abroad, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the talks. The firm met potential investors in Dubai and Istanbul in recent weeks to discuss a loan that could combine Islamic and conventional financing.

The domestic prize is a smaller import bill: Turkey spent USD 61.6 bn on energy imports in the first 10 months of 2026, up 19.4% y-o-y and already close to the USD 62.5 bn it spent in all of 2025, Trade Ministry figures show (pdf).

TPAO has tapped Gulf banks before: Kuwait’s KFH Capital, Emirates NBD Capital, and Standard Chartered coordinated its debut five-year sukuk in February, with First Abu Dhabi Bank, Dubai Islamic Bank, and Mashreq also helping arrange the sale. The state-owned producer initially raised USD 1 bn.

BACKGROUND- In Iraq, TPAO agreed in July to buy 15% of BP’s Kirkuk redevelopment venture. It also took a stake in Oman’s Block 80 which OQ operates, and signed agreements to explore two Repsol-operated blocks in Libya.

w2Traders who kept Gulf crude moving through Hormuz during the war want more of Qatar's barrels next year. Some of the world's biggest commodity traders approached QatarEnergy this month for 2027 term supplies of its Qatar Marine and Qatar Land grades, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the discussions. QatarEnergy usually sells most of its annual crude directly to refiners. Since the war began, though, some refiners have been reluctant to take on Hormuz transit risk, and trading houses have stepped in to arrange tankers, manage the shipping exposure, and deliver the crude to end buyers. Nothing has been signed yet, and the new contracts take effect in January.

ICYMI- Adnoc is holding similar talks with traders over 2027 supplies of its Upper Zakum, Das, and Umm Lulu grades. Traders are already getting these barrels to Asia. Vitol recently sold 1 mn barrels of Qatar's Al-Shaheen to an independent Chinese refiner, and Mercuria placed 2 mn barrels of the UAE's Upper Zakum with another buyer.
The war has cost global markets some 2.8 bn barrels of oil and 60 bcm of gas from the Gulf, according to the International Energy Agency’s (IEA)’s estimate in its World Energy Outlook (pdf).

items.t: Abu Dhabi World Jiu-Jitsu Awards honour 2026 champions
sum: The awards ceremony marked the close of the 18th Abu Dhabi World Professional Jiu-Jitsu Championship, which drew more than 10,000 male and female athletes from more than 130 countries.

Abdulmunem Alsayed Mohamed Alhashmi, Chairman of the UAE Jiu-Jitsu and Mixed Martial Arts Federation, President of the Ju-Jitsu Asian Union and Senior Vice President of the Ju-Jitsu International Federation, said the support and patronage of UAE President His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and His Highness Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi and Chairman of the Abu Dhabi Executive Council, had laid the foundations for a comprehensive sporting programme. He said its results could be seen in the achievements of champions, the development of sporting institutions and the growing number of people practising jiu-jitsu.

Alhashmi said the season’s results showed that the value of those achievements lay in the medals won and in the sustained development of jiu-jitsu in the UAE. He said the athletes reaching continental and world podiums had come through a system that identifies talent, trains athletes and helps them build the experience needed to compete at the highest levels.

He added that the Abu Dhabi World Jiu-Jitsu Awards recognise sporting excellence, reward commitment and sustained effort, and encourage academies and athletes worldwide to raise their standards. The awards also reinforce Abu Dhabi’s place as a key destination in the careers of jiu-jitsu champions, he said.

The ceremony recognised six Emirati athletes who excelled during the season. Ghayahib Al Rashidi was named best Emirati female athlete under 16, while Fahad Saud Al Dhaheri took the corresponding male award.
In the under-18 category, Zainab Mohammed Rashid Al Mansoori won best Emirati female athlete and Saif Issa Al Baloushi was named best Emirati male athlete.

In the senior category, Asma Hassan Al Hosani won best Emirati female athlete after a season of continental and world titles. Khaled Mohammed Al Shehhi was named best Emirati male athlete after winning gold at major international competitions, including the 62 kg black belt title at the Abu Dhabi World Professional Jiu-Jitsu Championship.

OG Capital clears the SPAC capital floor three months late
sum: OG Capital has cleared the EGP 100 mn capital floor for SPACs about three months after its deadline. Its board approved an EGP 90 mn increase on 18 November, taking issued and paid-in capital to EGP 100 mn through 100 mn shares at EGP 1 apiece, according to an EGX disclosure. Our friends at EFG Hermes ran the private placement behind it as promoter and underwriter, with First Abu Dhabi Bank Egypt as receiving bank.

IN CONTEXT- OG Capital listed temporarily in May and had until around 19 November to put an acquisition to a shareholder vote, with no target yet named. Its Financial Regulatory Authority-approved information memo sets the ambition at up to USD 500 mn in hospitality, automotive manufacturing and distribution, building materials, and healthcare. Its peers are late too — Grova placed 15 months after listing, and only Catalyst Partners Middle East has closed anything, two acquisitions worth EGP 2.8 bn.

Aman Holding is eyeing an EGX listing of 20% of its shares in 4Q 2027, the fourth date Raya Holding has set for it. The non-bank lender is in talks with two of Egypt’s largest IPO managers but has named no advisors, and CEO Hazem Moghazi says the timing rests on the company’s readiness, the market’s capacity to absorb the offering, and investor appetite, Alborsa reports. Raya first floated a 2021 debut in 2020, pushed it to 2023 with a bank already hired, then said it would not happen before 2H 2024.

EgyptAir will fly daily to Damascus from 4 December and four times a week to Aleppo starting 6 December, restoring direct flights suspended since 2011. The schedule follows a technical and operational protocol Egypt’s Civil Aviation Ministry signed with Syria’s General Authority of Civil Aviation last Wednesday, which activates their bilateral air transport agreement and lines up safety and operational procedures with international standards, according to a cabinet statement. Both routes will use Boeing 737-800s, EgyptAir said, as Egyptian contractors and exporters position for Syria’s reconstruction push.

Abu Dhabi investment delegation targets US partnerships in New York
sum: A senior Abu Dhabi delegation is in New York for a series of investment and business meetings aimed at expanding partnerships with US investors, financial institutions and companies.

The visit is being led by the Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO) and Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ADCCI), with representatives from Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development (ADDED), Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ADCCI), ADGM, and First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB).

At the centre of the programme is the second New York edition of the Abu Dhabi Investment Forum, taking place on Thursday, which will connect US investors and businesses with government and economic institutions from the emirate.
Discussions will focus on opportunities in financial services, artificial intelligence and advanced technologies, manufacturing, food innovation, infrastructure and urban development.

Badr Salim Al-Olama, Director General of ADIO, said the visit was aimed at deepening strategic partnerships with investors and leading US companies, while showcasing Abu Dhabi as a base for businesses looking to expand into regional and global markets.
The programme also includes meetings between Abu Dhabi private-sector companies and senior US business executives, with a focus on advanced manufacturing, agrifood and food security.

The forum returns to New York following its 2025 edition, which formed part of a wider visit that resulted in agreements across digital infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, financial services and new energy.

items.t: Abu Dhabi delegation connects US investors with opportunities in key sectors through high-level business engagements in New York
sum: The Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO) and the Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ADCCI) will lead a series of high-level investment and business engagements in New York to advance partnerships with US investors, financial institutions, and companies, and explore commercial opportunities across Abu Dhabi's priority sectors.

The visit forms part of Abu Dhabi's continued engagement with major international centres of capital, business, and innovation, positioning the emirate as a base for companies to develop new capabilities, establish operations, and expand into regional and global markets.

The delegation will bring together senior representatives from Abu Dhabi’s government and business ecosystem, including Abu Dhabi Department of Economic Development (ADDED), Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ADCCI), ADGM, Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO), and First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB).

The Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ADCCI) will organise its Global Executive Connect (GEC) programme on 18 November 2026, facilitating high-level engagements that connect Abu Dhabi’s private-sector companies with senior executives from leading US businesses. The programme aims to support practical business partnerships in sectors including advanced manufacturing, agrifood, and food security, unlock trade and investment opportunities, and help Abu Dhabi companies access new markets and expand internationally.

Through meetings with US investors and business leaders, the delegation will explore opportunities across financial services, artificial intelligence and advanced technologies, advanced manufacturing, agrifood and food innovation, infrastructure, urban development, and other sectors supporting the emirate's economic diversification.

As part of the visit, ADIO will convene the second New York edition of the Abu Dhabi Investment Forum (ADIF) on 19 November. The forum will connect US investors and businesses directly with Abu Dhabi's government and economic ecosystem, providing access to sector opportunities, institutional partners, and pathways for market entry and commercial expansion.

Dubai and Abu Dhabi companies post Dh77.5b in Q3 profits, up 12.7%
sum: ADX firms’ profits surge 19%, DFM firms’ earnings up 3.4%, led by telecoms, energy, realty

Dubai: Companies listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX) and the Dubai Financial Market (DFM) earned combined profits of Dh77.5 billion in the third quarter of 2026. This against the Dh68.7 billion it reported in the same period a year earlier, results in a rise of 12.7 per cent.
So far, 134 companies have reported their Q3 earnings with 73 on ADX and 61 on DFM. Of these 71 posted higher profits, 51 recorded declines and 12 booked losses.

Foreign companies haven't changed much to the headline numbers. Without them, combined profit reached Dh75.46 billion, against Dh71.18 billion in the third quarter of 2025. This reflects a growth of 6.01 per cent and shows that companies continue to post profits despite the varying performance of companies and sectors.

ADX-listed companies generated the larger share. Earnings climbed 19% to Dh48.37 billion from Dh40.65 billion (YoY). Excluding foreign names, profit rose 19.69% to Dh47.28 billion. 38 companies grew, 28 declined and 7 made losses.

One deal dominated headlines and added a big chuck to the overall profits. Etisalat earned Dh11.24 billion in the quarter, against Dh2.99 billion. The result includes a gain of about Dh8 billion from the sale of its Vodafone stake. Without that gain, net profit rose 7 per cent. Revenue climbed 6.9% to Dh19.5 billion.

ADNOC Gas posted net income of $1.34 billion, double the previous quarter’s level. EBITDA rose 70 per cent from the second quarter to $2.03 billion. The board approved a quarterly dividend of $940 million, up 5 per cent, payable in December. The company managed to post robust results despite being impacted by the disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.

UAE stocks decline on weak corporate earnings
sum: Stock markets in the United Arab Emirates closed lower on Friday, with industrial and financial stocks leading the decline as corporate earnings fell short of market expectations.

Dubai’s main market index declined 0.6%, retreating from a near five-month high touched in the previous session. Blue-chip developer Emaar Properties dropped 4.5%, while toll operator Salik Company slipped 2.5%.
Salik Company’s third-quarter net profit decreased 8.5% to 341.1 million dirhams ($92.88 million), while Q3 revenue declined 5.7% year-on-year.
Among losers, Dubai’s budget carrier Air Arabia slumped 1.2% following a 42% drop in its third-quarter net profit to 383 million dirhams ($104.29 million).
Abu Dhabi’s benchmark index fell 0.6%, snapping a four-session winning streak, weighed down by a 2.2% decrease in Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, while its largest lender, First Abu Dhabi Bank, dipped 0.8%.
Alternative investments firm Investcorp Capital declined 4.7% after reporting an 83% fall in first-quarter net profit to 2 million dirhams ($544,573.33).
The Dubai and Abu Dhabi indices recorded weekly gains of 2.9%, according to LSEG data.

sum: First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB) announced that its Board of Directors has approved a proposal to raise up to Dhs15 billion through a strategic rights issue, subject to the required shareholder and regulatory approvals.

The proposed issue will provide additional capacity to support FAB’s next phase of growth in the UAE and across its international network, while maintaining the capital strength, liquidity and financial flexibility underpinning its medium-term ambitions.

Since 2020, FAB’s total assets have increased by more than 50 per cent to Dhs1.4 trillion, while net income has doubled to Dhs21.1 billion. Return on tangible equity (RoTE) has risen by 6.2 percentage points to 19.2 per cent.

Between 2020 and 2025, the bank distributed Dhs44 billion in cash dividends to shareholders, representing nearly 20 per cent of all cash dividends on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX), while maintaining its AA- credit strength.
Over the same period, FAB expanded its international presence, becoming the first bank from the Middle East and Africa to establish a global banking franchise.
The Group now operates across more than 20 markets, connecting clients through 25 UAE-linked trade corridors.

The proposed rights issue aims to strengthen FAB’s ability to capitalise on growth opportunities in the UAE and internationally, deepen client relationships and support continued investment in strategic capabilities, including technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

UAE's biggest bank FAB to raise $4.08bn to boost next phase of growth strategy
sum: First Abu Dhabi Bank plans to raise Dh15 billion ($4.08 billion) through a rights issue as it prepares for “the next phase” of its growth strategy across the UAE and its global portfolio.
The UAE's biggest bank will be offering 1,109,467,456 new shares, with each to be offered at Dh13.52, a 30 per cent discount on its closing share price on Tuesday, a FAB statement on Wednesday said.

“The UAE continues to advance an ambitious long-term economic agenda, underpinned by diversification, investment, innovation and a growing role in global trade and capital flows,” said Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, chairman of FAB.

“FAB is at the centre of this growth, enabling strategic investment across the UAE and internationally. The proposed rights issue will further strengthen FAB’s ability to support the UAE’s ambitions and capture the opportunities ahead.”
The rights issue is also meant to capture “significant opportunities” in the UAE and across FAB's international network, group chief executive Hana Al Rostamani said.
Aside from the Gulf, FAB also maintains a presence in the Middle East, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.
“The strength of our home market, combined with the reach and connectivity of our international network, gives us a strong platform for growth,” Ms Al Rostamani said.

sum: First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB) announced it has fully acquired Bahrain's Yasira, a financial services platform specializing in fund administration and custody, in a strategic step aimed at strengthening the bank's ability to deliver integrated... solutions.

The acquisition will combine Yasira's fund administration expertise with FAB's leading regional custody capabilities, strengthening the bank's ability to give asset managers and institutional investors integrated solutions spanning public and private markets in the region and beyond.
The Yasira platform supports a wide range of investment strategies, including public assets, private equity, venture capital and real estate, across multiple entities, structures and jurisdictions.
The platform supports private funds throughout their life cycle, from investor commitments to capital calls, distributions and final financial reporting.

The deal will allow FAB to expand its existing custody services and offer more comprehensive solutions to investment managers regionally and internationally, with a particular focus on meeting the growing and complex needs of the Middle East's fund industry.

ADNOC Distribution profit surges 37% on record fuel volumes
sum: Net profit hits Dh2.90b as record fuel volumes and 71 new stations drive 9-month growth
Abu Dhabi: ADNOC Distribution’s net profit rose 37 per cent year on year to $791 million or Dh2.90 billion in the first nine months of 2026, the Abu Dhabi-listed fuel retailer reported on November 9.

EBITDA climbed 26 per cent to Dh4.10 billion or $1.12 billion. Underlying EBITDA grew 14 per cent to Dh3.47 billion or $944 million. Gross profit increased 20 per cent to Dh6.12 billion or $1.67 billion .
Fuel volumes reached a record 11.86 billion litres, including 8.26 billion litres through retail. Non-fuel retail (NFR) gross profit rose 13 per cent to $217 million or Dh797 million.
The board also approved a third-quarter dividend of 5.14 fils per share, worth $175 million or worth Dh643 million. Full-year 2026 dividends are expected to exceed $700 million.

Chief Executive Officer at ADNOC Distribution, Engineer Bader Saeed Al Lamki says the results show the company’s push into higher-margin businesses. “We are building on this momentum to future-proof our growth by scaling higher-margin NFR opportunities and progressing our international strategy,” he said.

He pointed out how its foray into South Affrica is being viewed as a change in the company’s identity. The group is “transforming into a leading international mobility and convenience retailer,” Al Lamki added.

Modon Closes USD 3.7B Syndicated Loan to Fund Development Pipeline
sum: Abu Dhabi-based real estate company Modon Holding secured USD 3.7 billion in financing. Thus, strengthening its liquidity position and extending its debt maturity as it advances its development pipeline.
The AED 13.7 billion facility combines a five-year term loan and a three-year revolving credit line. This is with an additional AED 4 billion accordion option.

The financing gives Modon greater financial flexibility to support its expansion plans without relying solely on new borrowing. By refinancing existing facilities and securing additional funding capacity, the company can manage its debt obligations over a longer period while maintaining resources for upcoming developments.

For investors and businesses operating in Abu Dhabi’s real estate and infrastructure sectors, the transaction also highlights the financing capacity available to large-scale developers as they pursue growth opportunities.
The facility is particularly significant for Modon because it represents the largest financing transaction in the company’s history.

The AED 13.7 billion (USD 3.7 billion) syndicated facility is structured across two tranches. It includes a AED 4.7 billion five-year term loan and a AED 9 billion revolving credit facility with an initial three-year maturity, which can be extended to five years.
The agreement also includes an additional AED 4 billion accordion option, allowing for potential expansion of the facility.

sum: ABU DHABI, UAE — Preparations are complete for the 18th Abu Dhabi World Professional Jiu-Jitsu Championship, with organizers expecting more than 10,000 athletes from 130 countries at Mubadala Arena in Zayed Sports City from November 9 to 21, 2026.

The championship will offer a prize pool exceeding AED 3 million, with more than 5,000 competitors expected to travel from outside the UAE.

sum: Dubai, UAE – The Dubai Financial Market index rose by about 1.8% to the level of 5,932.67 points in early trading, Wednesday. Meanwhile, the Abu Dhabi Securities Market index rose 0.95% to 9,553.41 points.

The gains were supported by strong jumps in real estate and banking stocks, especially Emaar shares. Following Emaar Properties’ announcement of its intention to submit an offer to acquire all of the shares it does not own in Emaar Development.
In the Dubai market, Emaar Properties» shares rose 4% to AED 12.24, and Emaar Development shares rose 5% to AED 14.6.

The company explained in a statement on the Dubai Financial Market that the offer amounts to 15 dirhams in cash per share. It is subject to the required approval from the Emaar Properties Board of Directors.
Emaar Properties’ ownership in Emaar Development currently stands at 79.16%. While all shareholders own the remaining 20.84%.
The number of Emaar Development shares is 4 billion shares. The 20.84% to be acquired constitutes approximately 833.6 million shares.
According to the aforementioned price (15 dirhams per share), the total value of the shares to be acquired amounts to approximately 12.5 billion dirhams.

Coal India's arm files IPO papers with Sebi; promoter to offload shares
sum: The proposed IPO is entirely an Offer For Sale (OFS) of up to 66.81 crore equity shares by its promoter Coal India with no fresh issue component, according to the Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) dated November 1.
Since the issue is entirely an OFS, SECL will not receive any proceeds from the offering, with the entire proceeds going to Coal India.
Incorporated in 1985 and headquartered in Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, SECL is among India's largest coal producers.
It produced 176.29 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for 16.94 per cent of the country's total coal production, DRHP said citing a Crisil report.
SECL's coal production increased 5.25 per cent to 176.29 million tonnes in FY26 from 167.49 million tonnes in the preceding fiscal.
The company was accorded Miniratna Category-I status in March 2007 and completed 40 years of coal mining operations in 2025.
As of April 1, 2026, SECL had total coal geological resources of about 47.55 billion tonnes, accounting for around 11.50 per cent of India's total coal geological resources.
